summary: Theodor Nöldeke was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. He studied at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald and Theodor Benfey, as well as Vienna, Leiden, and Berlin. He later held professorships at Göttingen, Kiel (1864–1872), and Strasbourg (1872–1906).

Indologist Theodor Zachariae studied at Leipzig under Georg Curtius and Hermann Brockhaus, Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and Hermann Sauppe, and completed his habilitation at Greifswald. He became a professor at Greifswald (1883) and comparative linguistics professor at Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).

Working in linguistics and other fields, Theodore Dwight Woolsey studied at Hopkins School, Yale, and Princeton. He served as president of Yale University (1831–1871) and president of the American Oriental Society (~1861–1881).
Theodore Riccardi works in Indology and linguistics. He served on the faculty at Columbia University, where he is attested as Professor Emeritus by 2026.
Theodorus Willem Juynboll studied at Leiden University from ~1886 to 1893. He later held an academic post at Utrecht University in 1916.
Working in linguistics and Indology, Theophil Gubler completed his doctoral degree at the University of Basel by 1903, having studied under Jacob Wackernagel.
Thi Xinh Nguyen, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed a PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).
Indologist Thibaut d'Hubert has held academic posts at the University of Chicago and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026 as Vertretungsprofessor).

Scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy Thich Nhat Hanh studied at Báo Quốc Temple, Saigon, Princeton, and Columbia. He taught at Columbia (1961, 1963–1964), Van Hanh University (~1964–1966), and Cornell University (~1966–1967).
Thich Thien Nghiem, a specialist in Buddhist studies, earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under doctoral supervisor Shalini Singhal (attested 2012).
Working in Tibetology and related fields, Thierry Mathou studied at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po. He has served as an Associated Political Scientist at the CNRS.

Thierry Meynard specializes in Sinology and philosophy. After completing his PhD at Peking University under Yulie Lou (~1999–2003), he became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University (~2006) and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies (2012).

Thinh Canh Quang, a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed a PhD at the University of the West (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda Warnasuriya, having also studied under Lewis Lancaster and Ananda Guruge.

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Thinley Dorji Bhutia served as Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, and as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).
Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, who worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Mindrolling Monastery and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (Dudjom Rinpoche).

Indologist and religious studies scholar Thomas A. Forsthoefel studied at Georgetown, Loyola University Chicago, and the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths. He became an associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University (attested 2007).

Scholar of religious and Buddhist studies Thomas A. Tweed completed his PhD at Stanford University (~1980–1989) under William R. Hutchison and others. He later served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).

Thomas B. Ellis, working in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Appalachian State University (attested 2009).

Thomas Blom Hansen, a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, studied at Aalborg University. He held posts at Natal, Edinburgh, Yale, Amsterdam (~2003–2010), and Stanford University, where he became Professor of Anthropology in 2010.

Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Thomas Borchert pursued PhD studies at the University of Chicago (attested 2005). He later became Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).
